paragraphs: Swamiji spoke from his own experience: one day the longing for a calm, peaceful life, where everything helps the mind to grow, will awaken in each of us. It may take countless lifetimes, but it is certain to come. When it does, hold on to it. Such a strong longing could not arise unless what you long for already exists for you. Still, he added, not every desire is the same kind of desire.
To show the difference, he told of a master who assured his disciple that if he truly longed for God, God would come to him. The disciple did not really grasp what this meant.

One day the two went to bathe in a river. The master told the boy to dive under, and he did. Instantly the master pressed down on him and held him beneath the water, not letting him rise. Only when the boy had fought until he was worn out did the master release him.

Gasping, the boy was asked how it had felt down there. All he could think of, he said, was a breath of air. The master asked whether he longed for God like that. The boy admitted he did not. Then the master told him that when he wanted God with that same desperate intensity, he would surely find Him.
learn: Casual wishing rarely changes anything; breakthroughs come when we want something the way a drowning person wants air. Ask yourself honestly how intense your desire is for the goals you say matter most.
